chapter: Split, hospital and decline of tap
title: Why Joe Steele was called Peckin': heel work and music appreciation
summary: The interviewers ask whether the nickname came from heel work; Green says Steele called it music appreciation and credits a Conway for the pecking step.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: I love it. You say his name was Pecking Joe Steele. The nickname, Pecking --
Joe.
Yes, is it anything to do with, like, wood pecker, pecking? I know you use your heels so much, you know, he uses his heels -- or did use his heels.
Yes.
So much so that it's, you know, it gives you the impression of a wood pecker pecking, you know, how they do.
Yes. Well, he calls it rapid tap.
Yes, the heels are rapid. He uses many of them.
I thought his name was Pecking Joe Steele because of him doing a dance called Peckin'.
Yes, that's true. That was his entrance -- that was his appearance. He appears pecking, you see, and --
I'm familiar with that.
He says, 'Where's my hat, where's my sombrero?'
Do you think he -- did he create this step, the pecking -- that pecking step which I'm familiar with -- did he create that because of his nickname, or was it already --
I think it was a gentleman called Conway --
Conway -- Tom Conway. He used to be in Conway and Parks.
He decided to use the pecking because of his nickname?
He used to do it --
Or did he use the step and then they gave him the nickname?
Well, he gave himself that.
I'm just wondering if the tap dance using the heels like had anything at all to do with the nickname, Pecking, because I know you do use an awful lot of heels in that.

Yes, he calls that -- what do he call that? He says he's got a title for it -- he says -- music appreciation. That's what he calls it -- music appreciation, see, dropping of the heels (unintelligible) like say, for instance, if you're playing staccato, see, and you go into what you call the overtone, you know, the tone like that -- the heel represents the tonal, you know, the front of the music -- it's like a foundation, see -- the heel.
The heel was the foundation of his work.
Yeah.
His tap work --
(unintelligible) I can see that.
Yeah.
It just seemed, you know, using that
nickname as well, often they do give people nicknames because of their style of work or something.
That's true, that's what happened to him.
You know, and --
Yeah, that's true. That's exactly --
Rapid heel work, as you call it.
Yes, yes.
